The wind chill is the temperature, in degrees Fahrenheit ( ${ }^{\circ} \mathrm{F}$ ), a human feels based on the air temperature, in degrees Fahrenheit, and the wind velocity $v$, in miles per hour (mph). If the air temperature is $32^{\circ} \mathrm{F}$, then the wind chill is given by $W(v)=55.6-22.1 v^{0.16}$ and is valid for $5 \leq v \leq 60$.\\
(a) Find $W^{\prime}(20)$. Using correct units, explain the meaning of $W^{\prime}(20)$ in terms of the wind chill.\\
(b) Find the average rate of change of $W$ over the interval $5 \leq v \leq 60$. Find the value of $v$ at which the instantaneous rate of change of $W$ is equal to the average rate of change of $W$ over the interval $5 \leq v \leq 60$.\\
(c) Over the time interval $0 \leq t \leq 4$ hours, the air temperature is a constant $32^{\circ} \mathrm{F}$. At time $t=0$, the wind velocity is $v=20 \mathrm{mph}$. If the wind velocity increases at a constant rate of 5 mph per hour, what is the rate of change of the wind chill with respect to time at $t=3$ hours? Indicate units of measure.
